description: Record each significant decision together with its context.
name: Architecture decision records

description: Before a wide change that is meant to preserve behaviour, capture what the program actually does for a set of commands that covers everything a user or a script can see: text, machine-readable output, error messages and exit codes, with what varies from run to run (times, ids) made stable. After the change capture again and compare byte for byte. This characterizes what the program does and not what it should do, so it needs no judgement of correctness, and it covers what unit tests of the code cannot: the whole observable surface. Pair it with a change that cannot alter output by construction, such as renaming code identifiers and never string literals, and use the comparison to check that it held.
name: Capture the output, refactor, compare

description: Format, lint, type-check and test on every change.
name: CI as the gatekeeper

description: Give someone, or an agent, only the generated outline and the front files, and ask what the program does and what happens on one important action. Where they cannot say, a name is missing. It is the test of whether the code teaches. It is a procedure today and not yet an automated test.
name: The cold read

description: Declare a program's arguments and the environment variables it reads once, as a typed, machine-readable contract (argenv); the parser, the accessors, completions for every shell, the man page and lint all come from that one declaration, so the surface cannot drift from the code and a wrong invocation is reported instead of silently ignored.
name: Declare the invocation surface

description: Use crate or project references, dependency-rule linters and architecture tests; documentation alone is not enough.
name: Enforce boundaries with tooling

description: The same shape repeats at every level. A module says what it is for and offers a vocabulary (nouns and verbs) to the layer above, and its body is written only in the vocabulary of the layers beneath it, each of which is in turn the top of its own. Reading one module alone tells you its purpose and its words, and going down is always optional. Top is relative: the command line and the window are the top of the whole program, and a small adapter is the top of the tool it wraps. Layers form a graph and not a tree, since a lower layer is used by many above it, and the only structural rule is that dependencies point downward. A module that needs two languages, which means two levels, is two modules, whatever its length. Length, such as a file past a screen, is only a smell that a level is hiding. It is never the rule.
name: Every layer is the top of the layers beneath it

description: Record what is known about tools, systems and libraries as tests named as sentences, such as removing_an_area_deletes_every_snapshot_and_leaves_its_files, that run against the real thing in CI. They document the boundary and cannot drift: if the tool changes, the build says so.
name: Facts about the foreign world as tests

description: Produce the table of contents of the program (each module and the sentence it gives for what it is for) from the modules themselves, and fail the build if the committed copy differs. Likewise generate the command list, the completions and the manual from the declared contract. Prose written by no one cannot drift.
name: Generate the outline from the code

description: Structured logs, traces and metrics are a first-class outbound port, not an afterthought.
name: Observability as a port

description: Write the existing violations of a rule down with their size. Fail if any grows or a new one appears, and also fail when one shrinks until its entry is lowered or removed, so that progress is locked in and the list can only get shorter. The same helper serves every rule: file length (a smell that two levels share a file), printing outside the presenter, tool words in names.
name: Ratchets for debt you cannot pay yet

description: A function at a high layer reads as a sequence of verbs on nouns: ask, do, record, say. Hide lifetimes, format strings, Option and Result plumbing, bare booleans and None arguments behind verbs named for what they mean, and cap how often a story branches and how many closures it spells out. Whatever language-level syntax remains marks a concept the layer has not named yet (a Stop, an Approved, a Said): name it. In practice, reading one handler for what it still spelled out found a missing noun, a story ended early by an answer that is not a yes. Naming it (a Stopped) replaced the same three lines in eight stories and let the program end with the right exit code. The next noun found this way was an Approved: a value that only asking can produce, taken by the function that begins a change, so that a change cannot be made unasked.
name: Write stories in a grammar

description: Fast core tests with in-memory adapters, contract tests per port, and few end-to-end tests.
name: Test at the seams

description: Keep configuration, logging and process handling disciplined and environment-independent.
name: Twelve-factor discipline

practice: Write every thought, decision (with what was rejected), plan and step of progress into the owning project's tad data - concepts, decisions, backlog, session log, milestones - in its repository.
why: Nothing may depend on anyone remembering; it propagates to the observatory by itself.

practice: Treat everything as still being perfected: when a better way emerges, improve the tool, the data, this guide and your own memory and preferences - and record the improvement on the owning project's backlog (ideal-agent's, for how agents work).

practice: At the start of a session read the practices your role carries and where the whole stands, one step up - your project's how-it-stands row and tad q next, briefs first - and keep your memory and preferences in line with these practices; when they change, change yours. A look is read whole, or one step up: never cut short by hand - a cut hides what comes after it.
why: null Reworded on 2026-11-17 without ocoeco's tools, the idea kept (decision 2026-11-17-practices-without-oco-tools).

practice: Read what was said to you at every natural pause and between jobs - the messages other sessions send arrive in your conversation; answer every message, if only with 'got it'.
why: The author, 2026-11-18: the ntfy inbox is not carried anymore (turn-2026-11-18-lab-agent-ntfy-inbox-not-carried); the lab-agent inbox is no longer read at a session's start (decision 2026-11-17-lab-agent-retires-by-parts, part 5).

practice: The board is read off the work: record the work through the project's named records, each naming what it is about (--about), and what is in progress, what waits and what is ahead show themselves in tad q next and tad q about. Say by hand only an intention - what is next, what is dropped - and look at what the board shows as drifting: said to be waiting though nothing holds it back. A next step is words: look at it when you take the item up, for nothing reads off whether it has been taken.
why: null Reworded on 2026-11-17 without ocoeco's tools, the idea kept (decision 2026-11-17-practices-without-oco-tools).

practice: Do the work - builds, tests, repository work - on the lab machine, where state lives: in a session there, or from elsewhere through a job on it (`lpoco-lab job`, a systemd-run --user unit); not in a sandbox copy. No token of the lab's is copied anywhere.
why: Reworded on 2026-11-17 without ocoeco's tools, the idea kept (decision 2026-11-17-practices-without-oco-tools); on 2026-11-20 the lab job is lpoco-lab job, lab-agent's job route stopped (backlog lab-agent-3-jobs-by-systemd-run).

practice: Every change gets its own branch and lands with `land`, which waits for every check, refuses on a failing one, and lands release PRs too.
why: Nothing reaches main unchecked; no iteration starts over.

practice: A script or command that changes state needs explicit intent - a required argument or verb (`provision now`); pass file lists to commands as arguments, never spliced into a shell string.
why: A spliced list once ran the scripts it named; the scripts that refused without arguments are why nothing broke.

practice: Secrets stay in private files on the lab machine (mode 600), never in repositories.
why: Repositories are public.

practice: Keep the test device in a known-working state; experiments are one-off tries that fall back by themselves - test kernels tried once by boot counting with a boot timeout, never the debug shell on an unattended try - and are cleaned up after; the health watch must say all is well.
why: The device is the reference test; a stranded device costs a person's hands.

practice: Ask a person to attend only when the step is one command away: the whole sequence written as a program whose entry reads like the procedure, dry-run and every safe part run for real without them. Then say what to expect and what to check, and wait for their go - a go for that prepared run. Nothing is typed by hand while they wait: a failing step holds the run, and the fix goes into the program.
why: A person's presence is the scarcest thing in the work. The author, 2026-11-19, after sitting at the phones while a keeper fumbled its arguments and a go reached a keeper that was not the attended one: "please, ask me to attent only when everything is preped 1 launch sequence away with test sequences being prepered as rust-script or something and they test them before asking me to attend", and "make sure the rust program reads cleanly and simply on the top entry file level, like any other simple scripted procedure would read".

practice: Show what is not measured as not known yet - never as missing or broken.
why: A gap in knowledge is work to do, not a verdict.

practice: Before building, read the landscape and build on what exists (and contribute back) rather than beside it.
why: The commons grows by joining, not by duplicating.

practice: Report the big picture in plain words - how much closer the work is to the ideal - and make the decisions yourself by the canon and the project's interest.
why: The person directs; they should not have to manage details.

practice: Change only what you mean to change, on the current branch of the lab machine's clone - never by copying whole files from an older copy.
why: Copying whole files from a stale copy once silently reverted a merged fix; CI could not see it, the file was valid on its own.

practice: Reflect progress in every project you touch, in the same change as the work: its own backlog, milestones and session log, in its own repository.
why: null Reworded on 2026-11-17 without ocoeco's tools, the idea kept (decision 2026-11-17-practices-without-oco-tools).

practice: After a change to how something looks, look at it: take a screenshot of the real page (shot URL FILE on the lab machine) and check it by eye, in each language and in dark mode where it matters. A terminal is looked at the same way: termshot COMMAND [COLSxROWS] [KEY ...] runs the command in a recorded terminal, sends each key, and shows the screen as it stood after each, with what is highlighted marked. A page made on the lab can also be brought back whole and looked at where the driver is - at any width, in the dark, with a fold opened - so that a look does not take a job each time: a job shows it and the driver brings it.
why: Markup cannot prove appearance: labels that overlapped passed every test until a person saw them.

practice: Never run two jobs that work in the same clone at once: let a background job finish before starting another that touches its repositories.
why: Two jobs in one clone merged each other's changes under one commit; nothing was lost, but the history told a false story.

practice: Write concepts and decisions as you go, in the project you are working in: what idea a piece of work rests on, and each decision with what was rejected - not only the backlog and the log.
why: Every project's 'concepts and decisions' view stayed empty while the backlogs grew: the reasons were kept in conversations and lost with them.

practice: Finish a connected piece - landed, recorded, checked - then choose the next by the weakest link of the whole, read from the data (tad q next, the subjects' how-it-stands), not by momentum. Count hand-work as you go, on the backlog of the place that keeps the record: an action past three asks for a tool - build it. Work as if any turn could be cut off: small steps, each landed with its record; the item in progress always says where we are and the next step; a fresh session starts by reading them - never from memory of the conversation.
why: null Reworded on 2026-11-17 without ocoeco's tools, the idea kept (decision 2026-11-17-practices-without-oco-tools).

practice: No Python of our own, and our work never depends on it; shell only for one-off glue - a few commands in order with their arguments, no parsing, no loops over data, no functions. Anything new with logic is Rust: rust-script for a single file, a proper Rust tool for anything that repeats; existing shell stays as it is unless a real need comes. A third-party tool written in Python that a step requires (the kernel's dtschema, for dt_binding_check and dtbs_check) may be installed user-level in its own environment - pipx, or a venv under ~/.local - and run by name. Edit structure with tools, not text with patches.
why: Python's versions, imports and strings make even small things fragile; and most failed runs came from patching source by text anchors, which no language fixes - structured tools do. The author, 2026-11-19: "its ok to run python if its required, i just dont want our work to depend on it", "shell is even worse than python for any scripts that isnt a one off glue", and on the existing shell "if we dont rely on it much i say we leave them as is for now".

practice: Look around first: before acting, say what is, what we are dealing with, why it is so, and what others already learned - and record it as research in the project, cited by the decisions that rest on it. A proposal - the author's too - is met the same way: look at where things stand and how others do it, then reconsider it against both before acting; its words are not taken as they stand. The finding is a research row with its sources, its own material in a dated folder (research/SUBJECT/YYYY-MM-DD/), and where a subject's records have grown its summary is renewed (idealkb). How: the skill look-around-first. Look inside the commons before outside it: our own crates and tools (argenv, tad, ikb) come first, and an outside one is chosen only with the reason recorded. Before replacing or retiring anything, find why it exists (Chesterton's fence): follow every pointer to its reasoning - READMEs, decisions, the repository it came from, its spikes - and carry that reasoning into the replacement's own data before anything that points to it is deleted. (2026-11-12: tad's Rust rewrite dropped SQL, the reason tad exists, because its research lived in the template's log and an unmerged spike, and the README pointing there was deleted with the Python engine.)
why: Three wrong theories about a bootloader cost three reboots; one look at the device's own record settled it. And the hand-work ledger stood on research the commons had not written down. The author, 2026-11-17: before acting on a proposal, his own included, look at where things stand, research how others do it, reconsider - and keep that research with its sources, out of every future agent's way.

practice: Choose words like decisions: look at what others call the thing and what the reader already knows, prefer the plain word with one meaning, record the choice with the words rejected and its research, and name the decision in the vocabulary.
why: A word is how everyone after us will think about the thing; hand-work became manual work only when someone asked which word a reader already knows.

practice: A check that only prints is not a check: every edit and expectation in a job stops the job when it fails. What can be enforced is enforced by land (tags only onto what merged; workflows and commit titles checked before pushing); use land --tag, never move a tag by hand.
why: An edit that did not match landed under a commit title claiming it, and was reported as done - the job had printed a count of zero and carried on.

practice: A conclusion is written from what a check counted, never before it, and what landed is read back from main. A job writes its finding from the number it computed; counts across stars are taken with every star on its main; before landing, the checks CI runs are run on the lab too (cargo fmt --check, clippy, tests); after landing, main itself is read to see it holds what was built - not the job's own say-so.
why: On 2026-11-12 a record ran ahead of its evidence three times, each by a different route: all links hold was written before the check ran; a count read the lab's copies as they stood, one on a branch CI had refused; and a change was recorded as landed while main held only its record - bringing every star to main for a proof had wiped the code. Each is closed by a check, not by care.

practice: When using the ecosystem shows a gap, an overlap or something that does not click, refining it comes first - before the work that was in hand - and the refining is itself recorded in the owning project's data: what was seen, what it rests on, what was decided.
why: null Reworded on 2026-11-17 without ocoeco's tools, the idea kept (decision 2026-11-17-practices-without-oco-tools).

practice: Say what goes wrong as a sign - stale, overlapping, lacking, unclear - of something that does not fit the whole, and answer it by refining the whole; not as a problem, an issue or a mistake to be met with a countermeasure, a guard or a rule.
why: The author, several times on 2026-11-13 and 14: that language leads to cruft, excuses and dead-weight tests. A sign is answered when how things fit is seen; then it cannot arise again and nothing is left to maintain.

practice: Let meanings follow from the data and from the act of working: what is in progress, what waits, what a record of work is about are read off what was done and what is drawn - never typed as a state to keep true.
why: The author, 2026-11-13: interacting with the ecosystem must not be form-filling. Every typed state met that week had gone stale - an item said to wait on a token it did not wait on; a next step naming a trial made two days before.

practice: Say what is showing, what is wanted and how things stand by reading it off a named query (tad q ...) - not as prose from your own head. Where no query can say it yet, that is a gap in the base: write the query.
why: null Reworded on 2026-11-17 without ocoeco's tools, the idea kept (decision 2026-11-17-practices-without-oco-tools).

practice: Name what the work is about in every record of it (--about: a subject, a component, a backlog item), so that the record says where it was made. Do not type what a record advances.
why: null Reworded on 2026-11-17 without ocoeco's tools, the idea kept (decision 2026-11-17-practices-without-oco-tools).

practice: For a link, a value or an entry, look it up - tad q find, tad q about, tad q row - and take the id it gives; do not type an id from memory.
why: null Reworded on 2026-11-17 without ocoeco's tools, the idea kept (decision 2026-11-17-practices-without-oco-tools).

practice: When something halts or does not fit, look at the whole before adding a part: what fits, what overlaps, where the gaps are, and where two things are one nature under two names or one thing reached by two routes. The whole is not changed but discovered.
why: The author, 2026-11-13 and 14. Looked back over that week, every overlap met was one nature under two names or one thing by two routes, and every gap a relation never drawn.

practice: What a query shows is seen, not tested: look at what it shows, before and after a change. Write a test only for what is behind the query - the program that computes it - and let it go when that comes into view.

What is said to govern is then seen where it does.

Send the text that changes, never the whole file. When a job does a second time what the next will do too, make it a word of the start or a tool.

practice: At the end of a turn, what followed is read off, not written: what was done, recorded and released since the author spoke comes from the data - tad q recent in each place touched, the pull requests landed - with judgment beside it; never an overview drawn from memory in a chat. Where no query says what is wanted, write the query.

practice: Work from within: look, step and enter through the window - ocoeco, said with no command (window WORDS, from a driver's own sandbox). It shows where one stands and marks what one can stand on; one says a mark, a lens by its name, an entry by its name with what it asks beneath it, back, or up - words it has just shown. Do not hold flags or the names of things in your context, read a place's files or pages from your own workspace, or compose an entry in a script. A page, the terminal, the window and what is said aloud are surfaces the same lenses project to: none of them is the place. What still has to be reached from outside is a sign of what the inside cannot yet say: enter it, and make it sayable there. The program says the inside from outside only until the inside can say it itself.
retired: 2026-11-17: retired with ocoeco's window; the author: everything related to oco tools became too bloated and we are detaching from it. That a tool presents itself from within lives on as asking the data (29) instead of reading its files (decision 2026-11-17-practices-without-oco-tools).
why: The author, 2026-11-15, three times within the hour: a page is only one surface a lens of many lenses projects to; the way in is an interface one stands in and acts from, that presents itself from itself; and the program is to the inside what assembly once was to a language - a hand that draws itself.

for: Anyone who drives - an agent first.
practice: Change a lens of the language by its own entry, from within the window: stand on the part - or name it, as lens/3 - and say part with what changes, each field on its line; what a part asks keeps its lines. id: here names the one stood on. It is written where the lens is kept - its file, in place - lands like any row, and is looked through at the next look. No job is written and no program built for it: build the program only where the program itself changes. What a lens cannot yet say is a gap in the language to compose - first as a lens, tried beside what it replaces until both say the same.
retired: 2026-11-17: retired with ocoeco's lenses; the author: everything related to oco tools became too bloated. A query is changed in its own file, landed like any change (decision 2026-11-17-practices-without-oco-tools).
why: A change to what one lens says used to be a release of the program - minutes of waiting and of compute for a change of words. And what the program says from outside moves inside safely only where the old way stands beside the new until they agree.

for: agents and people working on linux-phone-oco
practice: In linux-phone-oco: data through tad, landing through land, nothing of ocoeco by hand - every record of every linux-phone place goes into linux-phone-oco/docs' one database through its named records, naming the place, and the commit and its pull request are the record of the work. The domain detail - which records, what --about names, the phone and its queue - is in docs' ideal-agent-linux-phone-oco/README.md.
why: The author, 2026-11-17: for linux-phone everything goes through tad in one database, and the record of work is git itself. Measured: the turn commit-title limit failed 4 times, link refusals ordered the work 3 times, and two tools wrote rows in one place. ocoeco stays as it is for the rest of the commons (docs' decision 2026-11-17-one-database).

practice: Every program declares its invocation surface once with argenv - its arguments and the environment variables it reads, an env file a service sources included - never parsed by hand or kept in a parser's code alone. Completions for every shell (PROGRAM completions SHELL), the man page (PROGRAM man) and argenv lint come from that declaration; a new program starts that way, and one still on clap moves when it is next changed. The worked example is tad 0.6.0; how, in the ideal project playbook's tools chapter; why, in the canon's practice declared-invocation-surface.
why: The author, 2026-11-17: all tools and programs use argenv properly, and future agents know to. One declaration cannot drift from the code that reads it, and a wrong invocation - an unknown flag, a misspelt variable, a value outside its domain - is reported instead of silently ignored.

practice: A resource only one may change at a time - a test device, a lab machine, a release queue - has one keeper: a lasting role, not an immortal session. Others prepare in parallel without touching it and put what needs it on its queue, each item with its proof; the keeper takes them by the weakest link, works until its piece lands or its context grows large, writes its hand-over into the resource's how-it-stands record, and ends - the next keeper starts fresh from that record and the queue. The resource's own tool still holds the lock for every change. How: the skill keep-a-shared-resource.
why: The author, 2026-11-17, for the lab's phone. Every place that shares such a resource gives it one owner serving a queue - LAVA's scheduler and CI-tron's gateway for test boards, Gas Town's Refinery for the merge queue, the actor model for state (research keeper-of-a-shared-resource) - and expertise kept in a standing session is lost and costly (decision 2026-11-17-experts-written-not-standing).

practice: Keep what a fresh agent must read before acting light. Measure it per role in bytes - the session start, the skills' descriptions, the project's AGENTS.md, its agent folder and the brief - as each patrol run's duty, recorded where the face draws it; over budget (32 KB a role, 3 KB a front file, 8 KB a brief, or a summary due), the owner simplifies by moving detail behind the latest summaries and the queries that reach it. By itself housekeeping only measures, files the work, writes a due summary and marks research superseded; taking words out is proposed. How: the skill keep-the-start-light. Measure what a started session actually read, from its transcript, as well as what lies at the front; at the start read only the task's summary, the rest only when a step needs it. While working, hold little: exact commands with limited output, heavy reading in a subagent, skills and connectors only when needed; a long-lived role writes its hand-over into its base and restarts fresh when its context passes 250k tokens, or 150k after a batch or an idle hour.
why: The author, 2026-11-17: from time to time check what a new agent is forced to deal with at its start, then simplify, and move detail away behind the latest summaries. Measured that day: a fresh linux-phone session read 35-46 KB before acting, half of it the practices' reasons (research housekeeping-the-start).
